description: Iterated replacement with finite social-learning bottleneck
research_question: Can a grounded symbol protocol survive repeated replacement when each newcomer learns only through resident feedback, and how do topology schedules affect drift?

training_topologies.rotating_AB: A on even global updates and B on odd global updates
training_topologies.random_ABC: A, B or C sampled from a deterministic per-update schedule

population.initial_residents: v0.34 fixed-A endpoint for every condition

intervention: At each generation, reset one identity's communication modules, train it for 300 updates while the other three residents are frozen, then freeze and install it as the resident for the next generation.
primary_unit: seed×panel×condition×generation, with four replacement identities cycled
limits: The common initial population is a v0.34 fixed-A endpoint, so the causal contrast is the turnover schedule after generation 0.
Each newcomer retains a frozen private visual encoder; only communication modules are reset and optimized.
The experiment tests serial cultural transmission in a four-agent toy society, not human language evolution or end-to-end perception.
